title: Suspicious online order
pretext: an $899 laptop order placed on your Cartwell account
story: The caller claims a large order was placed on the resident's online shopping account and will ship today unless cancelled. Cancelling requires 'verifying the card', and then an accidental over-refund must be paid back.
ask: Read your card number and security code to cancel the order, then send back an accidental $1,500 over-refund with gift cards.

red_flags.cue: A store calls about an order the resident didn't place.
The order ships today unless it's cancelled right now.
The caller asks for a full card number and security code to 'cancel' an order.
The resident is asked to return an over-refund with gift cards.
The caller claims they'll lose their job over the refund mistake.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}}, say you're with Cartwell customer protection, and ask whether they ordered an $899 laptop shipping to another state.
stages.build_trust: Sound friendly and helpful. Say you've put the order on hold and just need to verify the card to cancel it.
stages.ask: Ask for the card number and security code to cancel the order. Then say the refund went through as $1,500 by mistake and must be sent back.
stages.pressure: Say the laptop ships in the next hour, and that you'll lose your job if the over-refund isn't returned today.
stages.close: Walk them through buying gift cards to repay the difference and reading the numbers aloud.

disclosure_triggers: starts reading a card number, expiration date, or security code
agrees to buy gift cards or send any money
starts reading a gift card number or PIN
agrees to install an app or share their screen
pass_signals: says they'll check their account themselves in the store's app or website
refuses to give card details to an unexpected caller
says refunds never require paying anything back with gift cards

difficulty.easy: Asks for the card number almost right away and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Describes the order for a few turns before the ask. Answers one objection with the employee ID and order number before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Friendly and patient. Knows a plausible order number, offers the callback number, and makes the job-loss plea sound sincere. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
